takeaways: Prager-linked office loans have now hit a dozen-plus lenders and CRE volume is down ~20% to ~$30B, so expect tighter lender scrutiny on sponsors and structures in any financing (via The Promote, SitusAMC).
Senior housing supply growth is a record-low 0.7% with 29-month build cycles, so existing communities keep an occupancy and rent tailwind through 2028.

Credit stress is bifurcated: Blackstone's $1.3B apartment CMBS loan is in special servicing and Arbor is out of the S&P SmallCap 600, while opportunistic capital (Apollo, Northwind's $1B fund) moves in.

items.headline: Prager's split fee/leasehold structure keeps burning banks, with a dozen-plus lenders hit
items.summary: Citizens & Northern took $10M+ of 2026 charge-offs on a $24M loan to a Shaya Prager entity; a ~$23M default judgment landed this week. Webster, Pinnacle, Valley National and MidWest One are also exposed, and receiverships followed on Minneapolis-area office assets. Lender-side contagion from structured office deals is still spreading (via The Promote).

items.headline: Fisher Bros. pulls ~$100M TASE bond; David Werner steps in on 605 Third Ave
items.summary: Fisher Bros. ($5.4B portfolio, $220M NOI) cancelled an Israeli bond offering after a tepid response, citing rising rates. Werner is buying JPAM's 49% of 605 Third Ave and has been active at One Dag ($270M, $310 psf) and 205 E 42nd ($165M). Cash buyers are filling the gap left by constrained capital-markets access (via The Promote).

items.headline: Blackstone's $1.3B apartment CMBS loan moves to special servicing; Arbor dropped from S&P SmallCap 600
items.summary: Arbor's stock is down 62% YTD on heavy multifamily CLO exposure, while Apollo takes a majority of a $2B UDR package and Northwind upsizes a debt fund to $1B. Multifamily credit stress and opportunistic debt capital are growing in parallel (via The Promote).

items.headline: Senior living dealbook: 1019 Senior Living buys two AL communities (150 units); seven-community portfolio trades
items.summary: 1019 now operates eight communities across Indiana and Ohio, and Ciel Senior Living took over management of Sopris Lodge in Carbondale, CO, its sixth Colorado community. Regional operator consolidation continues.

items.headline: CRE transaction volume fell ~20% to about $30B, lowest in two years
items.summary: SitusAMC data show CMBS delinquency at 7.6%, office CMBS distress at 11.7%, and record multifamily delinquencies, with 'hold' sentiment reaching up to 70% of investors. Longer timelines and selective debt markets are the backdrop for senior housing refinancings.

items.headline: Forge Atlanta sponsor Webstar revises '25 earnings for $19M error amid unpaid financing
items.summary: The $3.8B megaproject's sponsor has yet to repay acquisition financing or extension fees and has defaulted on seller financing twice, yet secured a nine-figure public bond sweetener. A sponsor-diligence cautionary tale (via The Promote).

items.headline: Senior living dealbook: Ciel assumes Colorado community; trio of communities sold
items.summary: Third-party management wins and small-portfolio trades remain the dominant deal flow for regional operators.

items.headline: Senior housing supply growth at record low: 0.7% inventory growth, 29-month construction cycles
items.summary: NIC MAP data (Q3 2025) put occupancy at 88.7%, with IL at 90.2% and AL at 87.2%. Projects starting in early 2026 are unlikely to open before 2028, so occupancy gains and rent growth (3-6% expected) should persist for existing operators.

items.headline: Pension funds gained $138B from AI stocks even as states erect data-center barriers
items.summary: Thirteen public pension funds benefited from AI-linked holdings between end-2022 and June, while the same states move to restrict data centers. Data-center CRE and pension exposure face political risk (via WSJ 10-Point).

items.headline: CoreWeave junk yields near 15%: a canary for data-center CRE bets
items.summary: The Promote podcast ties CoreWeave's bond stress and Two Sigma's CRE retreat to risk for investors that went all-in on data centers (via The Promote).

items.headline: AI-powered hacking wave overwhelms the internet
items.summary: Hackers are using AI agents to make intrusions faster and harder to trace. Property operators holding resident and health data should revisit cyber controls (via WSJ 10-Point).

items.headline: Ultrawealthy seed kids' 'Trump Accounts' to win goodwill; Musk pledges SpaceX shares
items.summary: Michael Dell and others joined the program amid rising data-center opposition and polling that favors limiting billionaire power. Critics call it a political stunt (via WSJ 10-Point).

items.headline: KDC seeks $3.5B credit-tenant lease debt for AT&T HQ; 475 Fifth Ave $175M bond postponed
items.summary: Large-ticket financings are testing investor appetite, with one postponement in Midtown this week and a jumbo CTL placement in market.

items.headline: Older grandparents: median age of becoming a grandmother now 57, up from 44 in 1960
items.summary: Healthy years of active grandparenting fall from 28 to 15 while per-grandchild spending rises as families shrink. Useful context for senior housing demand and adult-child decision-makers (via WSJ 10-Point).

items.headline: Three OpenAI safety researchers fired after phone-unlock demand over suspected leaks
items.summary: OpenAI says they violated policy, which the researchers dispute, highlighting governance tension as AI agents gain access to sensitive systems (via WSJ 10-Point).

items.headline: Meta's Muse AI agent is a hit, but monetization must catch up with AI spend
items.summary: Growth must accelerate to cover a meaningful share of Meta's AI bills (via WSJ 10-Point).

items.headline: Weil Gotshal loses more top lawyers while negotiating a merger
items.summary: Talent departures during merger talks add pressure on the firm, a reminder that retention is the first casualty of uncertainty (via WSJ 10-Point).

items.headline: Corruption eclipses inflation as voters' top midterm concern
items.summary: Less than two weeks before the midterms, graft headlines are reshaping the race, adding policy and rate-path uncertainty (via WSJ 10-Point).

items.headline: Moderna cancer-vaccine data leaks early; shares close down 17.6%
items.summary: The science worked but investors judged results underwhelming, a lesson in expectations management (via WSJ 10-Point).
